AAIR-Vault/02-Frameworks-Standards-Regul: Forces the decision on which contexts and affected parties are in scope for impact assessment, and whether Map must complete before build starts or can run alongside it.
Forces the choice between integrating AI risk into the enterprise ISO 31000 process and running a parallel AI register, and who arbitrates when the two disagree.
AAIR-Vault/03-Domain-1-Governance-Framew: Forces the decision on which KRIs carry the appetite, what a breach triggers, and whether breach halts the system or only escalates.
AAIR-Vault/04-Domain-2-AI-Lifecycle-Risk: Forces the decision on which lifecycle stage owns each control gate, and whether a stage can be skipped for low-tier use cases or is mandatory throughout.
Forces the decision on who validates independently of the build team, and whether validation evidence gates deployment or merely informs it.
Forces the decision on which features get a proxy-bias audit, which fairness metric applies, and whether a failed audit blocks release or is accepted with written justification.
AAIR-Vault/05-Domain-3-Risk-Program-Mana: Forces the decision on which threat classes are in scope for this system type, and which are recorded as accepted exposure rather than controlled.
Forces the decision on AIBOM scope -- models, datasets, prompts, third-party APIs -- and the refresh cadence that keeps it usable during an incident rather than stale.
AWS-Well-Architected/01-Operational-Exce: Forces the decision on which anti-patterns are accepted as debt with a named owner and which are remediated this cycle, and who signs the acceptance.
Forces the choice between procedures as code and documented manual runbooks, and which operations must be reversible rather than merely recoverable.
Forces the decision on which failures earn a tested runbook versus documented tribal knowledge, and who owns runbook currency after each incident.
AWS-Well-Architected/02-Security/SEC-Ant: Forces the decision on which security anti-patterns block release and which enter the risk register, and where exception authority sits.
AWS-Well-Architected/02-Security/SEC-App: Forces the choice between gating release on SAST/DAST findings and reporting them advisory, and which severity threshold actually stops a deployment.
AWS-Well-Architected/02-Security/SEC-Des: Forces the decision on where least privilege and defence in depth are enforced architecturally versus checked at review, and what gives when either conflicts with a delivery date.
AWS-Well-Architected/02-Security/SEC-Ove: Forces the decision on data classification per workload, and whether the security baseline scales to the most sensitive field present or to the modal one.
AWS-Well-Architected/03-Reliability/REL-: Forces the decision on which reliability anti-patterns are acceptable at this service tier, and what evidence is required to close one out.
Forces the choice between automated recovery and human-in-the-loop failover, and how often resilience is actually exercised rather than assumed.
Forces the decision on which quotas carry headroom alerts versus being discovered at failover, and who owns increase requests before peak.
AWS-Well-Architected/04-Performance-Effi: Forces the decision on which performance anti-patterns justify rework and which are accepted latency, and what measurement settles the argument.
Forces the choice between technology selected on measured fit and technology selected on team familiarity, and what evidence is needed to overrule the latter.
AWS-Well-Architected/05-Cost-Optimizatio: Forces the decision on tagging discipline, budget ownership, and whether lift-and-shift waste is remediated or accepted as the cost of migration.
Forces the decision on which workloads scale with demand versus hold reserved capacity, and who is accountable for idle spend between reviews.
Forces the choice between continuous automated rightsizing and periodic manual review, and who accepts the performance risk when a resource is downsized.
AWS-Well-Architected/06-Sustainability/S: Forces the decision on which sustainability anti-patterns are measured versus assumed out of scope, and whether idle capacity is treated as a defect or as headroom.
Forces the decision on region selection and utilization targets, and whether efficiency competes with latency or reinforces the cost objective.
Forces the decision on whether environmental impact is a reported metric with a named owner or an unmeasured externality outside the workload's scope.
Forces the decision on utilization floors for compute and storage, and whether carbon and cost are optimized together or traded against each other.
